q: How do you deploy a long-running agent in production?
a: API creates a run and enqueues it; stateless workers execute the graph and checkpoint state (Postgres) after each step; progress streams via Redis pub/sub and SSE; workers autoscale on queue depth; tools are separate least-privilege services.
So a run survives worker crashes (resume from the last step instead of repeating tool calls) and can pause for human approval and resume later.

q: How do you stop an agent repeating a side effect on retry?
a: Idempotency keys derived from run ID + step for every write action, and check whether the effect already happened before retrying.

q: How do you control agent cost?
a: Step limits, per-run token/cost budgets, wall-clock timeouts, loop detection, small models for routing/planning, caching deterministic tool results.

q: What's the classic silent failure of queue-based agents?
a: Requests accepted but never processed because workers are down or stuck. Alert on queue age/backlog and worker health.
